_about.what: Damaged cities (Brian, 20 November 2026: "when you click the cities there should be a repair button to press to repair the damaged buildings from artillery, bomb runs, and attacks. the production output and money are diminished the more it is damaged so repairing is important but costs money to do so"). The grand campaign only, behind its switch (g.flags.damage, set by the interfaces when a new grand campaign begins). Each province's chief town carries a share of itself in ruins, in percent (flag dmg:<region>). Its factories, its land, its harbour and the seat of government there pay that much less, and so do its town buildings, until the holder pays to repair it. Oilfields and the factory districts outside the walls are not the town: the existing rules for wrecked prizes keep them.
_about.most: The most of a town that can lie in ruins, in percent. A town is never wiped out: a fifth of it always works.
_about.raid: A raid on a province's industry by day or by night ('bomb' or 'night'). 'full' is the bombers through (as fly() counts them, after accuracy and anti-aircraft guns) that leave 'points' percent of the town in ruins; fewer leave their share. By night the bombs fall on the town at large rather than the works, so each bomber through counts 'night' times over for the town.
_about.town: Bombs on a besieged town ('town'): 'points' percent at a full bombardment (siege.json bombard.raidFull bombers through), less for less.
_about.shell: Ships' guns: 'points' percent for a full shelling of a besieged town's defences (siege.json bombard.shellFull weight of fire), and 'cityPoints' for a shelling of the city's works ('city'), full at a weight of fire of 'cityFull'.
_about.guns: A besieging army's artillery: 'perDiv' percent a month for each division of guns (supplied; half unsupplied, as the siege counts them), never more than 'most' in a month.
_about.battle: A battle fought in the province, in percent: 'field' in the country round the town, 'streets' where the town's guard fights beside the field army (ruling 232) or a relief or sortie comes to its gates, 'storm' for an assault that takes the town, 'repulsed' for one that is thrown back. The attackers' artillery adds 'guns' a division, up to 'gunsMost'. A small fight does less: the whole only where 'full' divisions or more fought on both sides together, and never less than a quarter.
_about.repair: The price of repairing a town: 'months' of the money its damage costs it (the pay of its factories, land, harbour, seat of government and town buildings, at the holder's own rates, before the nation-wide gains and losses). Never less than 'least' production points. A repair is paid at once and done at once; the player may take it back, with his money, in the month he ordered it.
_about.ai: A computer nation (and a player's staff with the building desk) repairs out of a purse it fills with 'share' of its income in every month it has a damaged town, keeping 'reserve' production points in hand. It buys only a repair that pays for itself within the price's own 'repair.months' (never a floor-priced repair of a town whose damage costs it next to nothing, an occupier reading its occupied share), repairs the towns whose damage costs it most first, and does not rebuild on the front line: never a town under siege, one beside ground its enemies hold, or one hit in the last 'quiet' months.
_about.field: Airfields as targets (Brian, 22 November 2026; the design director's ruling of 22 Nov 05:55Z on air-battles/airfields/airfield-targets-design.md). The grand campaign's air war only, behind its own switch (g.flags.fields, which the interfaces set for a new grand campaign when 'on' is true: on as shipped in release 2 since 22 November 2026 18:27Z, when the design director read the gate A/B/C as holding). One state per province's airfield (fieldstate.ts): 'fsh:<id>' the runway shut (the month), 'flv:<id>' levels burned, 'fht:<id>' last hit, 'frp:<id>' a repair in hand (the month it was ordered), 'frc:<id>' the player's price in that month, 'afc:<id>' a concrete level built. A raid shuts the runway where the bombers through reach 'shut' of the room the field serves; every 'level' bombers through burn one level of 'room' aircraft, at most 'levels' a raid, never below one level. Aircraft destroyed on the ground: (bombers through + 'strafe' for each escort fighter through) x 'ground' x the radar chain's 'ground' x 'surprise' in the month a war opens between the two sides, at most 'mostGround' of those parked, shared by parked weight with a bomber counting 'bomber' fighters. Repair is paid at once: the runway opens at the next month's start and a burned level comes back each month after; a new hit cancels the repair in hand. 'price' is DERIVED from what a field costs to build (arsenal.json works.field and works.strip), not from the months of pay PR 19 prices a town by (a field earns no pay): the runway and each burned level, at a strip or a concrete field, never below 'least' (PR 19's repair.least). 'plough': the levels burned when an army ploughs up a field by order and under scorched earth. 'worth': what a hit is worth to the raiders, in aircraft, as the staffs weigh it: those destroyed, 'shut' for each aircraft grounded, 'level' for each level burned. 'ai.quiet': a staff repairs an empty field only when it has not been hit in that many months.
_about.worth: What a raid's lasting damage is worth to the raiders, in aircraft, as fly() and its forecast weigh what a raid achieves: this many for each production point a month the damage takes from the town. (A month's output stopped is worth 200 a factory: air.ts outputWorth.) At 0 the air staffs choose their raids as they always did, and the damage is a consequence of the raids they fly; at 100, in 16 grand wars nobody played (stop 3, seeds 17 to 32), they bombed towns more and Germany fell about four months sooner, so it stays 0 until a ruling asks for more.
